candidates.tagline: Chicago raised a bridge rated 'intolerable' for a dinner cruise — it got stuck open for 4 hours, so they hosed it with a fireboat.
candidates.story: Chicago's DuSable Lake Shore Drive bridge, already rated structurally deficient and 'intolerable' in federal inspections, was raised for the Spirit of Chicago dinner yacht on September 2, 2026, in 96°F heat; the steel spans thermally expanded, couldn't close, and a Chicago Fire Department fireboat had to spray thousands of gallons of water on the span to cool it back down — blocking all traffic for over four hours.
candidates.why_funny: Officials raised a bridge they already knew was broken, for a dinner cruise, in extreme heat, and the only fix available was to put a literal fireboat on the river to cool off the not-on-fire bridge.
candidates.alt: Aerial view from Sky 5 helicopter of the DuSable Lake Shore Drive drawbridge stuck in the raised position over the Chicago River with water spraying across the steel span from a Chicago Fire Department fireboat below

candidates.tagline: Anker's fix for 'I don't want to wear a sleep tracker': a $270 radar gun aimed at your bed all night.
candidates.story: Anker unveiled the SleepLab Pro at IFA 2026 in Berlin on September 5, 2026 — a $270 bedside speaker that replaces your sleep-tracking wearable by firing a 60GHz millimeter-wave radar beam at your body all night to monitor heart rate, breathing, and sleep stages from the nightstand.
candidates.why_funny: The solution to 'I hate sleeping with a device' is to replace the wrist device with a bedroom radar station — you still can't escape surveillance, it just moved three feet away.
candidates.alt: The Anker Soundcore SleepLab Pro bedside speaker/nightlight on a nightstand, showing its cylindrical white form with soft ambient LED lighting
